guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, sw_key_data_reg[1] is cleared to zero on the next clock edge.

When engine_stable is high, for each 32-bit word index j from 0 to MaxKeyLen/32-1, if reg2hw.key_share1[j].qe is true, the corresponding slice sw_key_data_reg[1][32*j+:32] is updated with reg2hw.key_share1[j].q.
When engine_stable is false (and not reset), or when a specific word's qe is false while engine_stable is true, the corresponding bits of sw_key_data_reg[1] retain their previous value.

assumptions.claim: engine_stable must be asserted only when it is safe to modify the secret key share1 register, i.e., the key is not actively used in a hashing/KMAC operation or any security-critical computation.
assumptions.risk: If engine_stable is erroneously asserted during a sensitive operation, the key share may be corrupted mid-computation, potentially causing secret leakage or incorrect MAC/digest.

assumptions.claim: MaxKeyLen must be a positive integer multiple of 32 that matches the bit-width of sw_key_data_reg[1] and the dimension of key_share1 arrays to avoid out-of-bounds indexing.
assumptions.risk: If MaxKeyLen is set larger than the declared register width or not a multiple of 32, word slicing will access illegal bits or miss key bits, leading to secret corruption or synthesis/simulation mismatch.

uncertain_points.claim: Individual qe handshake bits may be asserted across multiple clock cycles while engine_stable remains high, leading to partial update of sw_key_data_reg[1] (some words new, some old).
uncertain_points.cond: engine_stable high and qe not all active in same cycle
uncertain_points.risk: A subsequent hash operation started after engine_stable deasserts could use an incomplete key share, breaking secret sharing integrity and potentially leaking information through incorrect MAC outputs.

uncertain_points.claim: MaxKeyLen parameter is used directly in the loop bound; if its value exceeds the actual width of sw_key_data_reg[1], word-write accesses will be out of bounds.
uncertain_points.risk: Out-of-bounds write may corrupt adjacent storage or be silently truncated in synthesis, altering the effective key and compromising security.
